```odin
import fake "fire:backend/fake"
```

Simulated audio driver for tests and headless runs. It produces callbacks of
fixed or jittery size in any native format and plane layout, can loop
outputs back to inputs with a fixed latency, and can inject xruns, device
loss and format changes. See /design/backend/.

## Types

### Device_Spec

```odin
Device_Spec :: struct {
	id: string,
	name: string,
	input_channels: int,
	output_channels: int,
	sample_rates: []f64,
	buffer_sizes: []int,
	default_sample_rate: f64,
	default_buffer_frames: int,
}
```

One simulated device, as listed by enumerate. Strings and slices are borrowed
and must outlive the driver.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` |  |
| `name` | stable ID and display name |
| `input_channels` |  |
| `output_channels` |  |
| `sample_rates` | Hz; open accepts only these |
| `buffer_sizes` | frames; open accepts only these |
| `default_sample_rate` | Hz |
| `default_buffer_frames` | frames |

### Config

```odin
Config :: struct {
	devices: []Device_Spec,
	input_format: backend.Sample_Format,
	output_format: backend.Sample_Format,
	input_plane_channels: int,
	output_plane_channels: int,
	jitter_min: int,
	jitter_max: int,
	seed: u64,
	loopback_latency: int,
	input_latency_frames: int,
	output_latency_frames: int,
	threaded: bool,
	realtime: bool,
	start_ns: u64,
}
```

How the fake driver behaves. Start from default_config.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `devices` | nil = one 2-in/2-out device, id "fake:default" |
| `input_format` | native format of the input planes |
| `output_format` | native format of the output planes |
| `input_plane_channels` | Channels per plane. 0 = all channels interleaved in one plane; 1 = one plane per channel (non-interleaved). |
| `output_plane_channels` |  |
| `jitter_min` | Callback sizes. jitter_max == 0 → every callback is buffer_frames long. Otherwise sizes are uniform in [jitter_min, jitter_max]. |
| `jitter_max` |  |
| `seed` | seeds the jitter sequence |
| `loopback_latency` | < 0: inputs are silent. >= 0: output channel k reappears on input channel k this many frames later. Must be >= the largest callback. |
| `input_latency_frames` | Reported in Device_Format and used for the input/output timestamps. |
| `output_latency_frames` |  |
| `threaded` | Threaded mode runs callbacks on a thread of its own after start; otherwise the test drives them with `run`. |
| `realtime` | threaded mode: sleep one buffer duration per callback |
| `start_ns` | manual mode: host time of frame 0 (deterministic timestamps) |

### Fake

```odin
Fake :: struct {...}
```

A fake driver instance. Fields are internal.

## Procedures

### default_config

```odin
default_config :: proc() -> Config
```

Defaults: the built-in 2-in/2-out device, f32 interleaved, fixed-size
callbacks, no loopback, manual mode with start_ns = 1 s.

### create

```odin
create :: proc(cfg: Config, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> ^Fake
```

Makes a fake driver. Free it with backend.driver_destroy(driver(f)); that
frees `f` too. `cfg.devices` is borrowed, not copied. Control thread.

### driver

```odin
driver :: proc(f: ^Fake) -> ^backend.Driver
```

The backend.Driver to pass to backend.device_init. Owned by `f`.

### run

```odin
run :: proc(f: ^Fake, n: int) -> (frames: int)
```

Manual mode: run `n` driver callbacks on the calling thread. Returns the
frames delivered. Does nothing once unplugged or when not started.

### inject_xrun

```odin
inject_xrun :: proc(f: ^Fake)
```

The next callback reports a discontinuity.

### unplug

```odin
unplug :: proc(f: ^Fake)
```

The open device disappears: callbacks stop and Device_Lost and
Devices_Changed are posted.

### change_format

```odin
change_format :: proc(f: ^Fake)
```

The device reports a format change (as when another app changes its rate).

### callback_count

```odin
callback_count :: proc(f: ^Fake) -> u64
```

Number of driver callbacks delivered so far. Safe from any thread.

### last_output

```odin
last_output :: proc(f: ^Fake) -> (planes: []backend.Driver_Plane, frames: int)
```

The native output buffers of the most recent callback.
